items.finding: Successive peaks rise (28 then 35 cases); peak week 7 with 35 cases; total 176 cases over 12 weeks.
items.reason: Remember: rising successive peaks mean person-to-person spread, not a point source.

items.finding: Bell curve with mean = median = mode = 2800 g; low birth weight (below 2500 g) is 25.2% of births.
items.reason: Remember: in a normal curve the mean, median and mode coincide at the centre.

items.finding: Long right tail: mean 5.05 days, median 5 days, mode 4 days (mean over median over mode).
items.reason: Remember: with skew the median is the preferred average because the mean is pulled toward the tail.

items.finding: Pooled odds ratio 0.78 (95% CI 0.68 to 0.89) favours zinc; Verma 2022 and Khan 2023 cross the null line (1.0).
items.reason: Remember: a confidence interval crossing 1.0 means that trial alone is not significant.

items.finding: Asymmetric funnel with a gap at the bottom right: small imprecise studies with null or negative effects are missing.
items.reason: Remember: a hollow asymmetric funnel means small negative studies were never published.

items.finding: Curves separate after 4 months and stay apart: 24-month survival 76% (new regimen) vs 50% (standard); ticks mark censored patients.
items.reason: Remember: separation that persists means a sustained survival advantage, not a chance crossing.

items.finding: Area under the curve 0.83 (good test); the curve bows to the top-left; the marked point gives sensitivity 63% at 88% specificity.
items.reason: Remember: the closer to the top-left corner, the better the test discriminates.

items.finding: 90 true positive, 10 false negative, 80 false positive, 820 true negative: sensitivity 90.0%, specificity 91.1%, PPV 52.9%, NPV 98.8%.
items.reason: Remember: predictive values come from the row totals; sensitivity and specificity from the column totals.

items.finding: Score = education (1-7) + occupation (1-10) + income (1-12): 26-29 Upper (I), 16-25 Upper middle (II), 11-15 Lower middle (III), 5-10 Upper lower (IV), below 5 Lower (V).
items.reason: Remember: Kuppuswamy has three components, and only the income bands change with inflation.

items.finding: WHO classes: below 18.5 underweight, 18.5-24.9 normal, 25-29.9 overweight, 30 and above obese; the plotted adult at BMI 27.3 is overweight.
items.reason: Remember: 25 and 30 are the two cutoffs that separate normal, overweight and obese.

items.finding: Expansive pyramid with a broad base: ages 0-14 are 294,000 of 882,000; dependency ratio 58.9 per 100 working-age.
items.reason: Remember: a broad base means a high birth rate and a young, growing population.

items.finding: +2C to +8C from state store (walk-in cooler) through district store and PHC to the session site (vaccine carrier); freeze-sensitive DPT and Hepatitis B must never freeze.
items.reason: Remember: heat damages all vaccines but freezing kills DPT and Hepatitis B potency.
